nodes.label: Brief Inference / Design Read
nodes.rationale: Most LLM design output is bad because the model jumps to a default aesthetic instead of reading the brief; the skill mandates a one-line Design Read (page kind, audience, vibe, system) before any code, and at most one clarifying question when the read genuinely diverges.

nodes.label: The Three Dials (VARIANCE / MOTION / DENSITY)
nodes.rationale: Every layout, motion, and density decision is gated by three numeric dials (DESIGN_VARIANCE, MOTION_INTENSITY, VISUAL_DENSITY) inferred from the design read, so aesthetic intensity is an explicit configuration rather than an accidental default.

nodes.label: Python-Driven True Randomization
nodes.rationale: LLMs are statistically lazy and always pick the first layout option; the skill forces a simulated seeded Python random.choice() in a pre-flight design_plan to deterministically select hero architecture, typography stack, components, and GSAP paradigms, forbidding the same UI twice.

nodes.label: Creative Variance Engine (Vibe + Layout Archetype Dice Roll)
nodes.rationale: To never generate the same layout or aesthetic twice, the agent silently rolls a combination of one Vibe/Texture archetype and one Layout archetype per prompt, keeping outputs uniquely tailored while staying inside a premium design language.
nodes.norm_label: creative variance engine (vibe + layout archetype dice roll)

nodes.label: Double-Bezel (Doppelrand) Nested Card Architecture
nodes.rationale: Premium cards must never sit flatly on the background; an outer shell with hairline border plus an inner core with concentric smaller radius makes components read as physical machined hardware.

nodes.label: Warm Monochrome Palette + Muted Pastel Accents
nodes.rationale: Color is treated as a scarce resource used only for semantic meaning or subtle accents: off-white canvases, ultra-light borders, and highly desaturated pastel tags, actively rejecting generic SaaS gradients and heavy shadows.
nodes.norm_label: warm monochrome palette + muted pastel accents

nodes.label: Scan-Diagnose-Fix Audit Sequence
nodes.rationale: Redesigns must work with the existing stack — scan the codebase, diagnose generic AI patterns via a checklist audit, then apply targeted fixes in a priority order (font swap first, typography polish last) rather than rewriting from scratch, so functionality is never broken.

nodes.label: Issue Template Config (contact link to coffee table)
nodes.norm_label: issue template config (contact link to coffee table)

nodes.label: Wrong Coffee Data Issue Template (bilingual EN/SK)
nodes.norm_label: wrong coffee data issue template (bilingual en/sk)

nodes.label: uv sync --locked Lockfile Drift Guard
nodes.rationale: --locked fails the PR check if scraper/uv.lock has drifted from pyproject.toml (issue #114, e.g. a Dependabot pin bump that skipped the lockfile), catching drift in CI instead of uv silently rewriting uv.lock during the next scheduled scrape run where it previously surfaced as an unrelated git rebase failure on the data commit.

nodes.label: Lighthouse Budget Job (a11y hard gate)
nodes.rationale: Issue #63: accessibility is a hard gate (0.95) but performance/SEO are only warnings, because Lighthouse perf scores fluctuate several points between runs on shared CI runners and a flaky red X teaches people to ignore the check.

nodes.label: workflow_run Trigger for Scrape-Data Rebuilds
nodes.rationale: GITHUB_TOKEN-authenticated pushes (scrape.yml's data commits) never trigger on:push workflows, so pages.yml listens for the 'Scrape coffee data' workflow's completion instead, guarded by an if-condition so a failed/cancelled scrape doesn't trigger a pointless stale rebuild.

nodes.label: Site Deploy Failure Alert Job
nodes.rationale: Issue #61: a failed deploy silently leaves the last good build up — the scraper side escalates failures to issues but nothing watched the site side; this opens or comments on one stable-titled 'Site deploy failing' issue (same dedup pattern as scrape.yml's roaster escalation) so persistent breakage doesn't spam.

nodes.label: Roaster Health Escalation Step (3+ consecutive non-ok)
nodes.source_location: Escalate roasters non-ok for 3+ consecutive runs
nodes.rationale: Issue #28: a roaster stuck non-ok for 3+ runs is past 'one flaky week' and needs a human; the step reads data/scrape_status.yaml (just written by the scraper) and opens (or comments on, to avoid duplicate spam) a stable-titled 'Roaster health: <name>' issue per roaster via the gh CLI.
nodes.norm_label: roaster health escalation step (3+ consecutive non-ok)

nodes.label: Staged-Diff Commit Guard for Data Artifacts
nodes.rationale: Artifacts are git-added BEFORE diffing (staged diff) because a plain git diff never sees a brand-new untracked artifact (the first-ever scrape_status.yaml / price_history.csv) and would skip the commit that should introduce it; price_history.csv is added behind an existence guard since git add errors on a pathspec matching nothing.
nodes.norm_label: staged-diff commit guard for data artifacts

nodes.label: LLM Extraction Canary Step
nodes.rationale: Issue #62: runs one known-good fixture page through the real extraction pipeline and ::warning::s on drift — the model fallback (issue #42) catches errors, the canary catches silently wrong answers; one cheap API call, no crawling, never fails the workflow.

nodes.label: Lighthouse Scores: Perf 0.92 / A11y 0.96 / Best-Practices 1.0 / SEO 1.0
nodes.norm_label: lighthouse scores: perf 0.92 / a11y 0.96 / best-practices 1.0 / seo 1.0

nodes.label: Two-Phase Discover-then-Detail Scraping Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The old single-phase one-LLM-call-per-roaster design couldn't tell 'a product disappeared' from 'the whole roaster failed to load', couldn't skip LLM calls for unchanged pages, and couldn't represent multi-package coffees; the current design discovers URLs cheaply via crawl4ai prefetch=True (no LLM), then extracts per product. There is deliberately no separate data/index.yaml — removal detection diffs this run's discovered URLs against products.yaml in memory since prefetch discovery is cheap enough to redo fresh every run.

nodes.label: SHA-256 Hash-Gated Extraction
nodes.rationale: compute_page_hash() hashes the same MAX_MARKDOWN_CHARS-truncated markdown window sent to Gemini plus the raw WooCommerce variations JSON — not the full raw markdown — because dynamic page chrome below the window (carousels, viewer counts, stock countdowns) would otherwise flip the hash every run (issue #13), and a price change on a non-default variant never touches visible markdown so hashing markdown alone would gate that change away forever. Verified live: a second run over unchanged pages made zero LLM calls.

nodes.label: Unforced (Optional) extract_product Tool Call
nodes.rationale: Forcing the tool call was tried first and verified broken: the model fabricated plausible-looking products from category pages, the homepage, and non-coffee pages that slipped past the discovery filter, because a forced tool call cannot decline. Leaving tool_choice at 'auto' lets the model reply in plain text for anything that isn't a single coffee product page, and the decline is cached as not_a_product so it isn't re-sent every run.

nodes.label: Partial-Discovery Preservation (pagination_status)
nodes.rationale: Issue #22: a single flaky pagination fetch or a catalog exceeding MAX_PAGES would silently wipe every product only reachable from unvisited pages; failed_midway/capped pagination now surfaces as roaster status 'partial', where rediscovered products are processed normally but the drop-if-not-rediscovered step is skipped — an incomplete discovery pass must never be read as 'everything not rediscovered is gone'.

nodes.label: Mass-Delisting Guard (suspect status)
nodes.rationale: Issue #39: even a clean-looking discovery is treated as suspect when it would drop more than 50% of a roaster's ok/incomplete entries (min 3) at once — roasters delist a handful at a time, so a site redesign that still parses as a listing is the likelier explanation; only ok/incomplete priors count so a mass drop of not_a_product noise after a discovery-filter tightening doesn't trip it.

nodes.label: WooCommerce Variations Structural Extraction
nodes.rationale: Markdown only ever shows the currently-selected variant's price, so asking the LLM to read prices off markdown silently loses every other weight tier; extract_woocommerce_variations() parses the data-product_variations JSON attribute from raw HTML (embedded at page load, no browser rendering needed) into weight/price tiers, and normalize_product() trusts these over anything the LLM guesses.

nodes.label: SCHEMA_VERSION Forced Re-Extraction
nodes.rationale: The hash-gate only skips re-extraction when the stored entry's schema_version matches the current constant — there is no cached raw LLM output to replay against new normalization rules, so a rule change forces exactly one re-extraction of every pre-existing entry, after which hash-gating resumes.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — Slovak Coffee Map Project Instructions
nodes.norm_label: claude.md — slovak coffee map project instructions

nodes.label: Controlled Vocabularies (process / roast_type / origin / Blend sentinel)
nodes.rationale: Fields are translated to canonical English at scrape time regardless of source language; a multi-origin blend matching no single country gets the sentinel 'Blend' instead of staying null because it genuinely has no one source country to report, but an explicit blend flag never overrides a stated country.
nodes.norm_label: controlled vocabularies (process / roast_type / origin / blend sentinel)

nodes.label: Scrape-Status Observability (warnings / step summary / escalation)
nodes.rationale: Roaster-level statuses are deliberately silent by-design degradations (stale data kept, last_seen frozen, exit code 0), but nothing escalated them, so a roaster that quietly broke months ago just faded from the table with no one told (issue #28); data/scrape_status.yaml's consecutive_non_ok streak now drives ::warning:: annotations, a GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY table, and ::error:: escalation at a threshold of 3 consecutive non-ok runs.

nodes.label: Custom EN/SK i18n with Stable English Data Keys
nodes.rationale: Only rendered text changes with language — every data-origin/data-process/data-roast attribute and filter option value stays the canonical English key from products.yaml, so switching language never changes which rows match a filter; language persistence writes localStorage only on first visit or explicit switch, because writing on every load makes the destination page read back its own just-visited language and bounce.
nodes.norm_label: custom en/sk i18n with stable english data keys

nodes.label: Six-Colour Brand Palette (Toxic Orange / Black Kite / Garnet / Morning Snow / Amazon Mist / Aqua Mist)
nodes.rationale: No other brand colours are permitted — no greys, blues, greens, or off-palette neutrals; MD3 token values are a static hand-maintained snapshot in custom.css rather than plugin-generated (issue #121).
nodes.norm_label: six-colour brand palette (toxic orange / black kite / garnet / morning snow / amazon mist / aqua mist)

nodes.label: Two-Family Typography (DM Serif Display + DM Sans)
nodes.rationale: Exactly two families, never a third: DM Serif Display for display/headings/wordmark 'Slovak', DM Sans (300/400/500) for caps labels, body, and UI.
nodes.norm_label: two-family typography (dm serif display + dm sans)

nodes.label: 8px Spacing Grid
nodes.rationale: All spacing is a multiple of 8px from a fixed scale (4 8 16 24 32 48 64 96); arbitrary values like 10/15/20/36px are forbidden.

nodes.label: Logo Icon + Wordmark Lockup (coffee-cherry mark)
nodes.rationale: The coffee-cherry icon mark always renders in fixed Full colour · Dark styling regardless of page theme and never inverts; only four approved wordmark colour variants exist, chosen by background, and no second icon mark may ever be introduced.

nodes.label: The Table Is the Product
nodes.rationale: Every other surface (hero, docs, recipe pages) exists to support the filterable table, not compete with it; users arrive with a specific in-progress question and the site's job ends at linking out to the roaster's own shop — it never sells directly.

nodes.label: Data Honesty over Polish
nodes.rationale: Missing fields, stale timestamps, and incomplete/not_a_product states should read as trustworthy gaps rather than being hidden or smoothed over — an editorial tool earns trust by showing its limits.

nodes.label: coffee_origins.yaml — Canonical Origin Country Alias Table
nodes.norm_label: coffee_origins.yaml — canonical origin country alias table

nodes.label: Origin Alias Normalization (regions, Slovak/Czech spellings)
nodes.rationale: Regions unambiguously belonging to one country (Huila/Tolima -> Colombia, Blue Mountain -> Jamaica, Sumatra -> Indonesia) are listed as aliases so region-only pages resolve to a country instead of null (issue #106); 'bali' is deliberately NOT an Indonesia alias because substring matching would hit diacritic-stripped 'balíček' (bundle) and misclassify every coffee-bundle product; ambiguous multi-country region names like Yirgacheffe are deliberately excluded.

nodes.label: page_hash Hash-Gating
nodes.rationale: Every entry stores a sha256 page_hash of the fetched page; an unchanged hash skips the LLM extraction call entirely, making weekly re-scrapes cheap.

nodes.label: variant Tier Label
nodes.rationale: Present only when a product sells the same weight in more than one form (e.g. whole bean vs ground) — distinguishes such tiers; absent, never null, on every other tier.

nodes.label: Blend Metadata (blend / blend_origins, issue #91)
nodes.rationale: Present only on multi-origin blends whose origin stays the canonical 'Blend' sentinel; blend_origins is display-only composition of canonical country names. An incomplete blend still carries it.

nodes.label: reextract_attempts Counter (issue #36)
nodes.rationale: Counts how many times an unchanged page was re-extracted and still came out incomplete; absent means 0. The hash gate holds once it reaches MAX_INCOMPLETE_REEXTRACTIONS in scraper/scrape.py — lets a flaky extraction self-heal without re-paying LLM calls forever.

nodes.label: schema_version Stamp / Forced Re-extraction
nodes.rationale: Stamped on every ok/incomplete entry; bumped whenever normalization rules change in a way that would alter output for already-scraped pages. There is no cached raw LLM output to replay against new rules, so a stale schema_version forces exactly one re-extraction even when the page hash is unchanged, after which hash-gating resumes.

nodes.label: consecutive_non_ok Streak Counter
nodes.rationale: Per-roaster counter of consecutive non-ok scrape runs, reset to 0 the moment a roaster comes back ok; drives escalation (GitHub issue creation) at threshold so a silently broken roaster does not just fade from the table.

nodes.label: roast_type_urls Category Hints
nodes.rationale: Optional mapping of roast_type value to category URL for sites (Shopify collections, Shoptet categories) that only reveal a product's roast type through which category page links to it, never on the product page itself — used as a last-resort roast_type fallback.

nodes.label: Required metadata.city
nodes.rationale: city is required so every roaster can be placed on the roaster map (RoasterMap.astro / mapData.ts) — a roaster missing it used to silently fall into the 'not on the map yet' list instead of failing the scrape run; 16 roasters accumulated that way before the schema made it required.

nodes.label: scraper: playwright Opt-in
nodes.rationale: Opt-in per-roaster flag selecting crawl4ai's browser-backed crawler instead of the plain HTTP one, for JS-heavy storefronts that render their product grid client-side.

nodes.label: _data/coffees.sample.json Dev Fixture
nodes.rationale: Hand-maintained flat sample data selected via import.meta.env.DEV so local dev never depends on real scraper output; content updated to match the migrated schema (English origins, canonical process values).

nodes.label: MD3 Token / !important Retirement (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Retiring the ~150 --md-sys-color-* tokens and 111 !important overrides is the biggest and riskiest audit item: load-bearing for every still-Starlight-rendered page, so it must happen alongside (not before) finishing the Starlight-to-Layout.astro migration (issue #121).

nodes.label: Tailwind v4 Scoped to src/components/ui/*
nodes.rationale: Preflight is deliberately not loaded because it would reset typography/spacing globally across still-Starlight-rendered docs pages; theme re-pointed at the six Design.md hex values instead of shadcn's default zinc/slate palette.

nodes.label: Toxic Orange Rebrand (#6f4e37 → #FF6037)
nodes.rationale: The theme seed shipped as #FF6037 (Toxic Orange), not the coffee-brown #6f4e37 originally planned — a deliberate rebrand by the project owner during implementation, applied with the full named palette (Morning Snow, Amazon Mist, Black Kite, Aqua Mist, Toxic Orange, Garnet). The plan retains #6f4e37 as a historical record.

nodes.label: workflow_run Trigger Gap Fix
nodes.rationale: A GITHUB_TOKEN-authenticated push (scrape.yml's data commit) does not trigger other workflows' on:push — GitHub's guard against recursive runs — so the original pages.yml design never fired after a scrape. Fixed post-implementation (commit dbb8835, caught in whole-branch review) with a workflow_run trigger on scrape.yml's completion, guarded to only build on success. Ordinary human pushes were never affected.

nodes.label: Scoped Data-Commit Guard
nodes.rationale: The data commit uses a scoped git add of the data file (not -am) before the guarded commit so it can never sweep up unrelated working-tree state on the runner, and a no-change run doesn't fail the job.

nodes.label: Incomplete-Status Flagging Principle
nodes.rationale: A product missing origin/roast_type/weight_g/price is flagged status: incomplete with a missing_fields list rather than being silently published with nulls or dropped outright — bad data stays visible for debugging and is excluded from the site until fixed.

nodes.label: Same-Price-Different-Weights Collision Rule
nodes.rationale: If 2+ tiers have distinct weight_g but identical price, the whole product's packaging is untrustworthy (an extraction bug, not a real price) — the whole product is marked incomplete rather than dropping tiers piecemeal, keeping the bad data visible.

nodes.label: Variations JSON Folded into Page Hash
nodes.rationale: WooCommerce only shows the default-selected variant's price as visible text — a price change on another variant never touches the markdown, so hashing markdown alone would hash-gate that change away forever. The raw data-product_variations JSON string is folded into the sha256 page hash so price-only changes still bust the cache.
nodes.norm_label: variations json folded into page hash

nodes.label: Stable English Filter Keys
nodes.rationale: Only the rendered label changes with language: data-origin/data-process/data-roast attributes and filter <select> option values stay the raw English key from products.yaml, so applyFilters()'s equality checks are unaffected and switching language can never change which rows a filter matches. name and roaster (scraped proper nouns) are never translated.

nodes.label: localStorage Language Persistence
nodes.rationale: Starlight's LanguageSelect is purely URL-based with no memory, and a static site has no server to set cookies — so a small localStorage-backed inline head script redirects to the stored language's mirror of the current path (safe because every page has a 1:1 counterpart) and a delegated change listener stores new choices without redirect loops.

nodes.label: Canary Product Page Fixture (Colombia El Canario)
nodes.norm_label: canary product page fixture (colombia el canario)

nodes.label: EUR-per-100g Value Comparison
nodes.rationale: Compare value in €/100 g (price / weight_g * 100), not sticker price — a 1 kg bag routinely beats a 250 g bag by 30%+; when several coffees fit equally, prefer the better €/100 g since there is no roaster affiliation.

nodes.label: One-Sentence Ko-fi Support Nudge (issue #116)
nodes.rationale: The project is a free, ad-free hobby whose weekly scrape costs real money, so after a successful recommendation the skill may mention ko-fi.com/slovakcoffeemap once, in a single closing sentence — never before or instead of the recommendation, never repeated, and dropped entirely on troubleshooting or failed lookups; the roaster's buy link stays the primary call to action.

nodes.label: Pipeline Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Prices are read from the roaster's own page, never estimated or converted; incomplete products are hidden rather than guessed; stale data is flagged with a warning icon; delistings are respected on the next weekly run. Nobody pays to be listed and no roaster can edit their own data.

nodes.label: 9 Grams Coffee (Žilina)
nodes.rationale: 9gramscoffee.sk has no on-site catalog; products are scraped via the external coffeeart.me storefront category.

nodes.label: Spojka Roastery (Prešov)
nodes.rationale: Main site is a JS one-pager; the Shopify shop subdomain has the full static catalogue, and roast type is only revealed by collection membership (roast_type_urls).

Still keyed (empty) in products.yaml and scrape_status.yaml.

nodes.label: O datach (Slovak About the Data page)
nodes.rationale: States the dataset honesty principles: prices are read verbatim from roaster pages (never estimated or converted), incomplete products are hidden rather than filled with fabricated values, stale rows are visually flagged, and delisted coffees disappear on the next weekly run - independence and no pay-for-inclusion are the design intent.
nodes.norm_label: o datach (slovak about the data page)

nodes.label: AI vyber kavy (Slovak AI coffee-picker page)
nodes.rationale: Recommendations must come from the live public coffees.json dataset, never from model memory, so only coffees actually in stock at real prices are suggested; ties between candidates are broken by price per 100 g to stay roaster-neutral.

nodes.label: Espresso Ice Cubes (shared ingredient)
nodes.rationale: Brewed espresso is frozen into cubes ahead of time (3 cubes = one double shot) so cold drinks get full espresso strength without dilution from ordinary ice.
